name: WV-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Carol Miller running with large fundraising edge
No polls or expert ratings; markets price 98% Republican
model.rationale: Carol Miller is an incumbent in a deeply Republican district with a wide fundraising advantage, and prediction markets give her roughly 98% odds. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays near the baseline.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected incumbent scandal could widen uncertainty, but the structural Republican lean makes movement unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
West Virginia's first district is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of about 22 points toward the GOP. Carol Miller, the incumbent, is running for reelection and has raised roughly $1.7 million, far outpacing Democratic challenger Vince George, who has about $258,000 and no outside support. A Constitution Party candidate is also on the ballot but is not a factor.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, and prediction markets price Miller's chances at about 98%. The district's heavy Republican tilt and her incumbency make an upset highly improbable.
